scope: Recheck the 23 unresolved hypotheses for 12–13 November across the LV, LT and EE calendars; no new calendar day is researched.
note: Four LV hypotheses are resolved: Jevgenijs, Jevgenija, Jevgēņijs and Jevģēnijs. Nineteen remain explicitly unverified: 18 LV and 1 LT. Juozapotas gains a verified historical spelling/short-form record while its proposed origin remains open, including a documented source-calendar discrepancy. Existing 12–13 November reviewed histories remain in place. New resources include academic articles and a repository-held historical trend study, an exact curated name entry, primary sporting records, and official spelling/calendar PDFs. Source IDs link outcomes to the growing shared directory. Search snippets and failed spelling leads are recorded as limitations, not accepted facts. Raw files remain private and URLs are not displayed in the widget. Continue on codex/namedays-round4.

records.name: Juozapotas
records.facts_used: Exact Juozapotas with short forms Juozas and Potas appears on 14 November in the 1964 Tikiu Dievą calendar, reprinted in Salys 1983. The project calendar still uses 12 November.
records.hypothesis: Juozapotas may be connected with the spelling Juozapatas. This remains an unverified comparison: the source documents Juozapatas, not a correspondence between the two forms. Similarity alone does not establish a shared etymology or justify transferring a historical person’s biography.
records.reason: Exact historical usage is now established, but the proposed Juozapatas etymological bridge remains unverified. The widget adds the verified record separately inside the qualified hypothesis account.
records.uncertainties: Salys PDF p. 317 / printed p. 302 was visually checked: Juozapotas (Juozas, Potas) is on 14 November in the 1964 calendar, reprinted in 1983. Our supplied LT calendar uses 12 November. Neither this discrepancy nor a commercial Joseph/Josaphat comparison proves the origin.
records.next_steps: Use LT-VLKK and LT-LITUANISTIKA to find an authoritative exact-form etymology or an explicit Juozapotas/Juozapatas paired record. Historical calendar usage and short forms are already established; preserve the 14-versus-12-November discrepancy.

records.name: Jevgenija
records.facts_used: Recent personal-name research documents the relationship between Jevgenija and Jevgeņija, differing in the spelling n or ņ. Through Jevgeņija and Jevgeņijs this feminine name connects with the Greek eugenēs family, well-born or noble; the spellings’ attestation dates remain separate. Balode and Siliņa-Piņķe’s 2025 article records Jevgenija being given to girls during the twentieth century in Riga and especially Latgale. They compare it with Jevgeņija in Siliņš’s 1990 dictionary. Absence from the older dictionary therefore does not mean the spelling was unused then.
records.reason: Newly opened exact-form scholarship or a curated name entry establishes the relationship, with separately checked historical or professional evidence.
records.uncertainties: The 2025 article PDF/printed p. 6 and the 2024 article p. 304 explicitly distinguish Jevgenija from palatalised Jevgeņija while treating them as variants. The twentieth-century Riga/Latgale usage is a statement in the study, not an exact first-attestation year. No 1877/1899 dates are transferred.

records.name: Jevgenijs
records.facts_used: Name researchers Laimute Balode and Renāte Siliņa-Piņķe explicitly discuss Jevgenijs alongside Jevgeņijs and Jevgēnijs as renderings of Russian Евгений. The wider family leads to Greek eugenēs, well-born or noble. The relationship is supported by scholarship, beyond spelling resemblance. The Latvian Olympic Committee uses this exact spelling in its profile of judoka Jevgenijs Borodavko. It documents his participation in the men’s under-100-kilogram judo events at the London 2012 and Rio de Janeiro 2016 Olympic Games.
records.reason: Newly opened exact-form scholarship or a curated name entry establishes the relationship, with separately checked historical or professional evidence.
records.uncertainties: The exact forms in the 2025 dictionary article PDF p. 6 and the 2024 Latvian article p. 304 were visually checked. The 2025 identity study pp. 144–145 directly links them with Russian Евгений. The Olympic Committee uses exact Jevgenijs for Borodavko and confirms London 2012 and Rio 2016 judo participation. No 1876/1864 dates are transferred from Jevgeņijs.

records.name: Jevgēņijs
records.facts_used: The name guide separately documents Jevgēņijs as a Latvian form of Russian Yevgeniy, alongside variant Jevgeņijs. The family leads to Greek eugenēs, well-born. The evidence concerns the exact spelling with ē and ņ; it does not automatically establish every similar form’s origin. RFS football club’s match report dated 8 April 2026 names its goalkeeper Jevgēņijs Nerugals. The report describes RFS’s 1–0 away win against Jelgava. It provides a specific instance of this spelling in professional sport, rather than a date for the name’s first use.
records.reason: Newly opened exact-form scholarship or a curated name entry establishes the relationship, with separately checked historical or professional evidence.
records.uncertainties: The curated exact-form guide explicitly gives Latvian Jevgēņijs as a Yevgeniy form. The RFS match report dated 8 April 2026 uses Jevgēņijs Nerugals and records a 1–0 away victory against Jelgava. Other pages spell the same goalkeeper differently; this account describes the actual report spelling, without assigning it to another person.

records.name: Jevģēnijs

Figure 5 of the 2025 article Reflection of Identity in Given Names of Latvia Over the Last Century compares these variants’ popularity in Latgale using historical CSB data. It documents the spellings’ coexistence, rather than establishing one creation year or a combined present-day bearer count.
